# Dates and age {#sec-dd-dates}

```{r}
source("R/book.R")
cols <- dict_groups$dates
cs <- coverage_share(cols)
fu <- read_pipeline("outputs", "quality", "first_use_source.csv")
fu_n <- setNames(fu$n_vehicles, fu$first_use_source)
cv <- read_coverage("coverage_by_first_use_year")
yrs <- unique(cv[, c("first_use_year", "n_vehicles")])
n_odd <- sum(yrs$n_vehicles[!is.na(yrs$first_use_year) &
                              (yrs$first_use_year < 1900 |
                                 yrs$first_use_year > 2026)])
```

## Overview

A vehicle has several dates that mark the start of its life: when it was made,
when it was first registered, and when it was first used on the road. For most
vehicles these are within weeks of each other, but they can be years apart for
an import or a vehicle that sat in stock. @sec-lifecycle describes the stages
of a vehicle's life and how the data records them.

- **`first_use_date`** is the date to use for a vehicle's age: the DVSA first
  used date, else the DVLA month of first registration, else `birth_date`.
  `first_use_source` records which.
- **`birth_date`** is the earliest of the DVSA first used, registration and
  manufacture dates; for the few vehicles with none of these, it is taken
  from the DVLA dates, and `birth_date_source` records which. It decides
  when a vehicle is `unborn` in `pca_YYYY` (@sec-dd-location).
- **`final_test_date_DVSA`** is the date of the last recorded MOT test, and
  **`last_mot_year`** the year after which the vehicle is treated as `dead`:
  no longer observed, not necessarily scrapped (@sec-pitfalls).
  `last_mot_year` is the last year in which `is_end_use_YYYY` is `TRUE`
  (@sec-dd-location).
- **The MOT test dates as supplied** are carried through unchanged:
  `first_test_date_DVSA` and `first_test_year_DVSA` for the first test,
  `final_test_year_DVSA` for the last, and `lastMotTestDate_DVSA`. Use
  `final_test_date_DVSA` rather than `lastMotTestDate_DVSA`: DVSA put a date
  in the future in `lastMotTestDate_DVSA` for vehicles that have never been
  tested.
- **The supplied dates** (`_DVSA`, `_DVLA`) are kept as received. The DVLA
  month of first registration is accurate to the month only.

How these dates are built is set out in the methodology,
[section 3.2](../../reports/methodology.md#dates), and how the last MOT test
date is read in [section 3.5](../../reports/methodology.md#tidying). Other
DVLA dates, such as tax due and MOT expiry, are described with the licensing
status in @sec-dd-dvla-status.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-dd-dates
#| tbl-cap: "Date columns."
dict_table("dates")
```

## Coverage

Because three sources are combined, `first_use_date` and `birth_date` are
missing for almost no vehicles. `r fmt_pct(fu_n["firstUsedDate_DVSA"] / sum(fu$n_vehicles), 0)`
of first use dates are the DVSA first used date,
`r fmt_pct(fu_n["monthOfFirstRegistration_DVLA"] / sum(fu$n_vehicles), 0)`
the DVLA month of first registration and
`r fmt_pct(fu_n["birth_date"] / sum(fu$n_vehicles), 0)` the birth date.
A few dates are implausible: `r fmt_n(n_odd)` vehicles have a first use date
before 1900 or after 2026.

The coverage of the supplied dates follows their sources
(@fig-dd-dates):

- **The DVSA first used date and last test date** come from the MOT history,
  so they are present for tested vehicles only. Coverage falls sharply for
  vehicles first used since 2023, most of which have not had their first MOT:
  `r cov_year("firstUsedDate_DVSA", 2023)` for 2023 and
  `r cov_year("firstUsedDate_DVSA", 2024)` for 2024. The DVSA registration and
  manufacture dates are present for almost every vehicle.
- **The DVLA dates** are present wherever a VES record was found
  (@sec-dd-dvla-status). `monthOfFirstDvlaRegistration_DVLA` is different: it
  is present only for the `r cov_pct(cs, "monthOfFirstDvlaRegistration_DVLA", digits = 1)`
  of vehicles first registered somewhere else, such as imports.
- **The supplied first and final test dates** (`first_test_date_DVSA`,
  `first_test_year_DVSA` and `final_test_year_DVSA`) are present for
  `r cov_pct(cs, "first_test_date_DVSA")` of vehicles, those that have had an
  MOT test. `lastMotTestDate_DVSA` is present for more,
  `r cov_pct(cs, "lastMotTestDate_DVSA")`, because it also holds the future
  dates of untested vehicles.
- **`last_mot_year`** is blank by design for a vehicle that is still being
  tested, or that was last seen in the final two years of data. Its coverage
  is therefore highest for old vehicles, most of which have left the road, and
  close to zero for new ones.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-dd-dates-coverage
#| tbl-cap: "Share of vehicles with a value, by year of first use."
coverage_table(cols)
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-dd-dates
#| fig-cap: "Share of vehicles with a value in selected date columns, by year of first use."
#| fig-height: 4.6
coverage_plot(c("firstUsedDate_DVSA", "final_test_date_DVSA",
                "monthOfFirstRegistration_DVLA", "last_mot_year"))
```

## Values

How the values of each column change over time, by year of first use, from 1990. Numeric columns and
dates show the minimum, lower quartile (Q1), median, upper quartile (Q3) and
maximum; other columns show the share of vehicles with each value, with the
less common values grouped as *All other values* and missing values as
*Blank*.

```{r}
#| output: asis
cat(dict_values("dates"))
```
